subject: Immediate: head-of-line blocking & batch contention impacting ApexHealth latency

Date: 2027-11-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes — urgent

Hi Rishi,

We saw a sharp jump in 95/99 latency starting ~14:40 UTC and sustained errors (502/504) across multiple endpoints. Throughput dropped by ~40% while CPU/GPU util looked steady on our side. This is directly impacting our triage workflows — several users are timing out.

Attached is a short packet of request traces and the service-side error logs. We also noticed batching metrics show large queued batch sizes and many batches hanging for >150ms before tokens are emitted.

Can you confirm whether any config or KV/cache rollout happened this morning? We escalated to our ops and headed for an incident call if we don’t have a mitigation in 30 mins.

—Alex
A. Chen, Platform Engineering

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-11-28T15:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Production latency spikes — urgent

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for attaching traces. I’ve looped in the account team and on-call infra owners. Initial read: queued batch growth + long KV cache misses can cause exactly this symptom (head-of-line blocking).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share a short windowed export of request ids that experienced 502/504s (a few examples is fine).
- We’ll pull the tenant-level batch-size telemetry and KV hit/miss histograms; I’m asking Jonas to run a config snapshot compare.

Short-term mitigation we’re planning now (will execute in the next 10–30m after confirmation):
1) Roll back the KV prefetch tuning we rolled earlier this week for multi-tenant batching (if it’s active for APX).
2) Temporarily cap max batch size for ApexHealth to 8 tokens per request and enforce per-tenant batch isolation.
3) Enable a short-lived slot throttle (throttle new long-running batches) to break HOL blocking.

Marissa/Ben/Jonas/Naomi — please prioritize. I’ll coordinate the customer call.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 29, 2027 at 08:04 AM marissa.cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — quick update for the APX execs / account side: ...

Executed the short-term mitigation at 2027-11-29T08:17:22Z:
- Rolled back kv_prefetch_policy from "aggressive-shared" -> "balanced-per-tenant" for tenant APX-724. (See attached snapshot: kv-config-snapshot.txt)
- Set max_batch_tokens=8 and per_tenant_batching=true for tenant APX-724.
- Deployed slot-throttle at infra layer to limit concurrently queued batches per worker to 16 for APX-724.

Immediate observable impact (08:20–08:30 UTC window):
- p95 latency reduced from ~420ms -> ~160ms; p99 reduced from ~1.2s -> ~380ms.
- Error rate for routed endpoints dropped from 4.6% -> 0.8% in the first 10 minutes.
- Throughput normalized to ~88% of baseline (brief dip during config flip).

Notes and follow-ups:
- We saw several long-lived KV miss spikes coming from a small set of hot prefixes — likely configuration + dataset skew. Those prefixes are being throttled to prevent HOL blocking.
- We will snapshot logs and share a short diagnostic package to Alex (attaching logs).

Command snippets used:
- rwctl kv config --tenant APX-724 --set prefetch=balanced-per-tenant
- rwctl batching set --tenant APX-724 --max-tokens 8 --isolate-tenant true
- rwctl infra slot-throttle --tenant APX-724 --max-concurrent 16

I will keep the mitigation in place for 3 hours and then run a canary rollback with tighter observability.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-11-30T10:03:00Z
Subject: Executive summary & ask: ApexHealth HOL/blocking incident (status + recommendation)

Team / Alex — brief exec summary for leadership:
- Impact: 2027-11-28 14:40–11/29 08:20 UTC, ApexHealth experienced elevated p95/p99 latency and a 4–5% error rate tied to head-of-line blocking caused by aggressive shared KV prefetch + multi-tenant batch coalescing. ~2.2M requests affected; customer reports ~6k user minutes of degraded UX.
- What we did: rolled back KV prefetch to balanced-per-tenant, capped per-tenant batch sizes to 8 tokens, and applied infra slot-throttles. Those mitigations reduced p99 by ~70% within 10 minutes.
- Current state: mitigation active, monitoring. Will run a staged canary rollback after 3 hours with extra telemetry on hot prefixes.

Exec asks:
1) Approve up to $45k in one-time customer credit to ApexHealth for incident impact and to preserve the relationship (Marissa to finalize language).
2) Authorize an immediate postmortem task force (Jonas lead) with a 72-hour SLA to deliver: root cause, long-term KV strategy (per-tenant prefetch defaults), and runtime safeguards (prefetch safety checks and dynamic batch backpressure).
3) Approve prioritized engineering time to harden per-tenant isolation in the next sprint (2 engineers, 3 weeks).

If leadership agrees, I’ll prepare a short external-facing RCA and a talking points doc for Marissa to share with APX execs.

Thanks all — please reply with approvals or changes.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
